records.rationale: Correct comparison of REF and RREF: reduced form adds unit pivots and zeros elsewhere in pivot columns, and RREF is unique while REF is not. The prompt asks for the difference rather than an exhaustive shared definition.

evidence.title: NTNU, Gaussian elimination
evidence.finding: Echelon form requires pivots stepping right and all-zero rows at the bottom. Reduced echelon form adds unit pivots and zeros elsewhere in pivot columns.
For [[2,1],[0,3]], REF can retain nonunit pivots; row reduction produces the unique identity RREF. Zero-row placement is a shared echelon condition.
Both forms also require all-zero rows at the bottom. That shared condition is omitted from the brief comparison, but the distinguishing conditions are accurate.

records.rationale: The unimodular Smith-form description is sound, but the final determinant identity omits the square-matrix restriction. Smith form also exists for rectangular integer matrices, where the ordinary determinant is undefined.

evidence.title: Richard Stanley, MIT: Smith Normal Form and Combinatorics
evidence.finding: The square-matrix Smith form refines the determinant through its diagonal product; the construction extends to rectangular matrices, where no ordinary determinant exists.

A=[2,0] is a 1 by 2 integer matrix with a Smith form, but det(A) is not defined. For a square matrix the product of all Smith diagonal entries, including any zeros, gives the absolute determinant with nonnegative normalization.
The source calls the diagonal entries invariant factors, so do not assume it excludes zero entries. The hold concerns only the omitted square-A condition.
